messages:
Emily Zhang: Quick follow-up to the sampling RFC — I'm putting up a short proposal for 'sparse trace reconstruction' for LLM inference paths. goal: preserve accurate cost attribution for token-gen workloads without full trace retention.

Emily Zhang: Idea sketch: store a small set of deterministic markers and span-deltas for sampled requests (eg, first N spans, checkpoint spans at model boundary, and per-request token metadata). then an offline rehydration job deterministically reconstructs the full logical trace for billing/chargeback.

Jason Cole: Neat. how do you plan to handle prefix/KV cache hits? lots of tokens can be produced with zero model invocations after cache replay — attribution gets weird.

Emily Zhang: good call. plan is to capture "generate events" with a token_count and model_cost_estimate + cache_hit flag. rehydration will expand those into synthetic spans that attach cost to the original caller. not trying to fake latency, just cost lineage.

Priya Menon: Are we adding new fields to the envelope? that can be invasive for edge telemetry. we need a compatibility mode for older clients.

Emily Zhang: keep envelope tiny: add sampling_marker (string), sampled_span_snapshot (list of span ids + minimal attrs), and token_summary (token_count:int, cache_hits:int, model_variant:string). All optional fields. existing consumers ignore them.

Marco Ruiz: Storage tradeoff: storing token_summary per request is cheap, sampled_span_snapshot might still be large if we include stacky traces. can we limit snapshots to boundary spans only (ingest, router, model-call)?

Emily Zhang: exactly. boundary-only + hashed stack samples for root cause queries. snapshot size target < 1KB per sampled request. approximate cost calc on ingest for quick dashboards; exact rehydration runs async on a smaller subset for billing/audit.

Sasha Kim: One more constraint: customers on Private want no off-cluster rehydration. how would this work for Private deployments?

Emily Zhang: rehydration code will be modular. Hosted: RL job runs in analytics cluster. Private: rehydration runs customer-side (we ship the rehydration binary and manifest). models/keys never leave their cluster — only the sparse markers and token_summaries are used.

Jason Cole: Sounds reasonable. What about correctness guarantees? rehydration is deterministic only if we can replay the exact request path metadata (model variant, prompt hashing, batching decisions). batching is nondeterministic across time.

Emily Zhang: yep — we keep the minimal determinism set: model_variant, input_digest, batch_window_id (approx), and prefix-cache-version. For anything nondeterministic we mark the reconstructed spans as "approx" and fall back to conservative cost attribution (charge to request owner).

Priya Menon: Any perf impact on hot path? we can't add sync work.

Emily Zhang: all writes are async to the telemetry buffer. small sync write: sampling_marker header only. snapshots and token_summary are buffered. aim is <200B sync payload.

ingest-bot: note: sampling_marker schema v1 registered in registry. index: sampling_marker, token_summary.token_count, sampled_span_snapshot.boundary_type.

Marco Ruiz: then next steps? RFC + cost model for extra storage, and a compatibility test in staging.

Emily Zhang: I'll draft an RFC with data-size estimates, example envelope changes, and a rehydration reference (python). tagging @Jason @Priya for review. planning a 1-week async review, then a short sync on Thursday. :thumbsup:
